activities.summary: UAE ADGM sourcing pass: identified and disqualified as a direct-to-consumer digital wealth app rather than an institutional/family-office asset manager. Recorded with reasoning so this firm is not re-evaluated as a lead next quarter.

description: ADGM-regulated (FSRA Category 3C for managing assets, also Category 4 for advising/arranging) digital wealth platform, secured its licence mid-2023. Client assets are held at Interactive Brokers (IBKR), segregated, with SIPC/FDIC protection cited; delivery is via an app/digital platform to individual investors, with CFA/CFP-certified advisors described as fiduciaries. The business model (app-based, third-party custody, consumer-facing marketing comparing itself to a UAE retail bank's wealth offering) reads as a direct-to-consumer digital wealth/robo-advisory product rather than an institutional or family-office book-of-business needing a front-to-back PMS.

fit.disqualified_reason: Direct-to-consumer digital wealth/robo-advisory app (assets custodied at IBKR, marketed to the general public, compared against a retail bank's offering) rather than an institutional or family-office asset manager needing a front-to-back PMS — matches the ICP's retail/neobank consumer-product disqualifier. Revisit only if it pivots to a B2B/institutional model.
fit.reasoning: Fit ~20/60: FSRA-regulated (5) and UAE market (15) are real, but the business is structured as a direct-to-consumer digital wealth app (client assets at IBKR, general-public marketing, comparison pages against a retail bank) rather than a firm managing pooled or discretionary books for family offices/institutions in the sense the ICP targets — scored 0 for priority segment, multi-asset and third-party-by-way-of-business criteria. This matches the ICP's explicit disqualifier: 'a retail brokerage or neobank wanting a consumer product, not a management platform.'
